mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of similar high-rate regimes, or FEDFUNDS drops below 5% within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower labor market participation reduces risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 3.5% and remains >3.5 for next two months
regime_hint: rising unemployment or tighter labor market
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20/60-day windows during such UNRATE increases, or alternative proxies (e.g., PAYEMS) show opposite effect.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand (GDPC1) grows at a double-digit rate for two consecutive quarters, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as strong consumer and business demand boosts optimism.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate >10% in two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: No significant return in 20-day window during such events, or alternative demand proxies (e.g., HOUST) contradict.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO index below 100 for three months indicates contracting supply-side conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are non-negative in >40% of INDPRO contraction regimes, or alternative supply proxies (e.g., RSAFS) show opposite sign.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is negative due to immediate market reaction to higher policy rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase >0.5pp in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive in >70% of such events, or no significant effect detected in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in PAYEMS and UNRATE above their prior month levels indicate labor market weakness and suggest negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of such interaction events, or alternative proxies (e.g., GDPC1) contradict.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where CPIAUCSL inflation exceeds 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is negative due to market anticipation of tighter policy.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are non-negative in >60% of such inflation regimes, or alternative inflation measures (e.g., core CPI) show different pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When the interaction of INDPRO < 100 and RSAFS < 700 for two consecutive months occurs, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive as dual supply constraints boost risk premia.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 and RSAFS < 700 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >70% of such interaction events, or alternative supply/demand proxies (e.g., HOUST) contradict.
